text:
You told me: my father never wept;

you told me: my grandfather never wept;

the men of my bloodline never wept—

they were made of steel.


As you spoke, a tear welled up

and fell into my mouth… more poison.

Never have I drunk from another cup so small.


Weak woman, poor woman who understands:

I knew the pain of centuries as I drank it.

Oh, my soul cannot bear

all its weight!

translation.title: Ancestral Weight
translation.editorial_note: The inherited masculine prohibition becomes bodily poison; bloodline keeps raza familial rather than racialized.
